prompt: A burst leaves a FIFO queue full of jobs. Workers keep processing at a steady rate, while new jobs arrive more slowly and join the back. A teammate predicts the queue becomes empty as soon as the last job from the original burst finishes. What is wrong with that prediction?

options.text: Nothing: finishing the burst always empties the queue
options.explanation: Wrong. New jobs have joined behind the burst while it was being processed.

options.text: The burst can finish while later arrivals still remain
options.explanation: Correct. FIFO places new jobs behind the original burst. Emptying the entire queue takes longer because those jobs also need processing.

options.text: A queue can never recover once a burst exceeds capacity
options.explanation: Wrong. A temporary burst can be drained when later arrival rates stay below processing capacity.

options.text: New arrivals always delay the last original job under FIFO
options.explanation: Wrong. Under the stated FIFO and fixed-rate assumptions they join behind it; they delay the return to an empty queue.

workedExample:
1. Mark the jobs already present at the end of the burst.
2. Under FIFO, workers process those jobs before the new jobs joining behind them.
3. When the last marked job finishes, later arrivals can still be waiting.
4. Only spare processing capacity reduces the total backlog. As continuing arrivals approach processing capacity, emptying the queue takes longer; sustained arrivals above capacity prevent recovery.

prompt: A PDF-rendering queue grows during each working day and shrinks overnight, but every morning starts with more unfinished work than the previous morning. Assume no failed jobs, changing job sizes or retention expiry. What is the right diagnosis and response?

options.text: The workers cannot clear a full day's arrivals; increase effective capacity or reduce admitted work
options.explanation: Correct. Quiet hours are not making up the daytime deficit. Capacity needs headroom to clear the recurring workload and recover from incidents.

options.text: Load levelling is working because the queue shrinks overnight
options.explanation: Wrong. Shrinking for part of the cycle is insufficient when each complete cycle leaves a larger backlog.

options.text: Raise the queue's maximum size to solve the problem
options.explanation: Wrong. More storage delays overflow but does not change the accumulating capacity deficit.

options.text: FIFO ordering guarantees the backlog will eventually disappear
options.explanation: Wrong. Ordering determines which jobs run first, not whether enough jobs can be completed.

workedExample:
1. Compare the same point in successive workload cycles, rather than only the daytime peak.
2. A rising morning baseline means each day leaves unfinished work behind.
3. Increase effective processing capacity, reduce admissions or reduce work per job. Check downstream limits before adding workers.
4. Monitor oldest-message age and retention as well as depth; a queue cannot preserve unfinished work indefinitely.

link.title: Avoiding insurmountable queue backlogs (Amazon Builders' Library)
